summary: Verified requirements.txt fix for deployment ResolutionImpossible. requirements.txt (142 lines) has no duplicate package names (normalized case/-/_/.) and every package pinned with ==; google-auth only once at 2.56.2 (old file had both 2.52.0 and 2.56.2). `pip install --dry-run -r requirements.txt` exits 0 in the current venv AND in a brand-new fresh venv; `pip check` reports no broken requirements. litellm==1.80.0 resolves via the extra-index (emergentintegrations pulls the litellm wheel). Backend restarted via supervisor, startup clean. Core APIs pass: login (good + bad password), /api/auth/me, /api/branding, /api/dashboard/summary, /api/dashboard/pending-applications, /api/dashboard/trending, /api/dashboard/inbox. Regression test_iteration9_app_review.py passes 10/10 when run serially.

minor.issue: These paths from the review request do not exist (404 and 405). This is not a regression: the real routes are /api/dashboard/summary|trending|inbox|pending-applications, and those were tested instead.
Startup log shows 'EMERGENT_LLM_KEY not set — uploads disabled'. The key is missing from backend/.env. This is not caused by the requirements change, but it disables uploads.

action_items: Optional: set EMERGENT_LLM_KEY in backend/.env if uploads should work in preview.
Optional: test_iteration9_app_review.py is order-dependent and fails in parallel under xdist (pytest.ini probably enables -n). Run it with -n0 or make the tests independent.
critical_code_review_comments: requirements.txt is clean: all pinned, no duplicates, no direct-URL deps, and the --extra-index-url line is kept for emergentintegrations.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Only requirements.txt changed. Smoke test at tests/test_iteration10_requirements_smoke.py. Use -n0 for order-dependent older suites.
rca of the issue: The old requirements.txt had google-auth pinned twice (2.52.0 and 2.56.2), so pip could not resolve. The file was regenerated from pip freeze with a single pin of 2.56.2, which fixes it.
